_about: New Creation side by side (plan 7.6b): what more than one source says of a creation made new, and of a person made new, each in the passages' own words (Berean Standard Bible, every quotation machine-checked), with Alike and Different in the site's voice. Rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites for New Creation and seven reviewed Apocalyptic rows; the Alike and Different lines read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet): 18 accepted, 12 revised, none withdrawn (ontology/provenance/briefs/7.6b-NC-{DRAFT,REVIEW}.md). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the theme's subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words (Doug, 2026-10-06).
columns_note: The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi. Psalms & elsewhere: any other Old Testament book.

rows.title: New heavens and a new earth

The Prophets: I will create new heavens and a new earth
the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, will endure before Me
The letters: we are looking forward to a new heaven and a new earth, where righteousness dwells
Revelation: Revelation 21:1
Then I saw a new heaven and a new earth
Revelation 21:1
the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more

rows.alike: Isaiah 65:17 and 66:22 speak of "new heavens and a new earth" and "the new heavens and the new earth"; 2 Peter 3:13 and Revelation 21:1 both have "a new heaven and a new earth".
rows.different: Isaiah has "heavens" and God speaking ("I will create", "which I will make, will endure before Me"); 2 Peter has "we are looking forward to" and adds "where righteousness dwells"; Revelation has "I saw" and adds "the first heaven and earth had passed away, and the sea was no more".

rows.title: Heaven and earth wear out and pass away

The Prophets: the heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like a garment
they will all wear out like a garment
The skies will be rolled up like a scroll
Psalms & elsewhere: In the beginning You laid the foundations of the earth
They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment. Like clothing You will change them
Gospels & Acts: Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away
Heaven and earth will pass away, but My words will never pass away
until heaven and earth pass away
it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away
The letters: They will perish, but You remain; they will all wear out like a garment
You will roll them up like a robe
The heavens will disappear with a roar
Revelation: Revelation 20:11
Earth and heaven fled from His presence, and no place was found for them
Revelation 21:1
the first heaven and earth had passed away
Revelation 6:14
The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up

rows.alike: Isaiah 51:6 says "the earth will wear out like a garment", and Psalm 102:26 and Hebrews 1:11 say "they will all wear out like a garment"; Hebrews 1:11 has the same words as the first part of Psalm 102:26. Matthew 24:35 says "Heaven and earth will pass away" and Revelation 21:1 that "the first heaven and earth had passed away". Mark 13:31 and Luke 21:33 have Matthew 24:35's words. Isaiah 34:4 says "The skies will be rolled up like a scroll" and Revelation 6:14 "The sky receded like a scroll being rolled up".
rows.different: What remains differs: "My salvation will last forever" (Isaiah 51:6), "but You remain" (Psalm 102:26; Hebrews 1:11), "My words will never pass away" (Matthew 24:35); Psalm 102:27 goes on "But You remain the same, and Your years will never end". Hebrews 1:12 has "You will roll them up like a robe", which Psalm 102:26 does not, and "like a garment they will be changed" where Psalm 102:26 has "Like clothing You will change them"; 2 Peter 3:10 has "The heavens will disappear with a roar", Revelation 20:11 "Earth and heaven fled from His presence", and Revelation 21:1 "had passed away". Matthew 5:18 and Luke 16:17 speak of the Law: "until heaven and earth pass away", "easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law".

rows.title: The former things passed away; all things new

The Prophets: Do not call to mind the former things
Behold, I am about to do something new
The former things will not be remembered
Behold, the former things have happened, and now I declare new things
proclaim to us the former things
I foretold the former things long ago
Gospels & Acts: in the renewal of all things
The letters: The old has passed away. Behold, the new has come!
Revelation: Revelation 21:4
the former things have passed away
Revelation 21:5
Behold, I make all things new

rows.alike: Isaiah 42:9, 43:19, 2 Corinthians 5:17 and Revelation 21:5 each say "Behold" before something new: "I declare new things", "I am about to do something new", "the new has come", "I make all things new". Isaiah 42:9, 43:18, 65:17 and Revelation 21:4 speak of "the former things", and 2 Corinthians 5:17 and Revelation 21:4 both say what is old or former "has passed away" or "have passed away".
rows.different: Isaiah says "Do not call to mind the former things" and that they "will not be remembered"; Revelation 21:4 says they "have passed away". Isaiah has "I am about to do", Revelation "I make", and 2 Corinthians "the new has come", said of "anyone" who "is in Christ"; Matthew has "the renewal of all things" and Acts "the restoration of all things".

rows.title: Created new: heavens, a heart, a person

The Prophets: I will create new heavens and a new earth
I will create Jerusalem to be a joy
Psalms & elsewhere: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me
The letters: if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation
What counts is a new creation
to create in Himself one new man out of the two

rows.alike: Each speaks of creating or of a new creation: "I will create new heavens" (Isaiah 65:17), "I will create Jerusalem to be a joy" (Isaiah 65:18), "Create in me a clean heart" and "renew a right spirit" (Psalm 51:10), "a new creation" (2 Corinthians 5:17; Galatians 6:15), "to create in Himself one new man" (Ephesians 2:15).
rows.different: What is created differs: "new heavens and a new earth" and "Jerusalem" in Isaiah; "a clean heart" in the one praying in Psalm 51; "anyone" who "is in Christ" in 2 Corinthians; "one new man out of the two" in Ephesians. Isaiah speaks as God ("I will create"), the Psalm asks God ("O God"), and Galatians sets "a new creation" against "circumcision nor uncircumcision".

rows.title: Death swallowed up; no more death

The Prophets: He will swallow up death forever
Where, O Death, are your plagues? Where, O Sheol, is your sting?
The letters: Death has been swallowed up in victory
Where, O Death, is your victory? Where, O Death, is your sting?
The last enemy to be destroyed is death
so that our mortality may be swallowed up by life
Revelation: Revelation 21:4
there will be no more death
Revelation 20:14
Then Death and Hades were thrown into the lake of fire

rows.alike: Isaiah 25:8 says "He will swallow up death forever" and 1 Corinthians 15:54 "Death has been swallowed up in victory"; Hosea 13:14 asks "Where, O Sheol, is your sting?" and 1 Corinthians 15:55 "Where, O Death, is your sting?". Revelation 21:4 says "there will be no more death".
rows.different: 1 Corinthians 15:54 calls its words "the saying that is written"; Hosea pairs "plagues" and "sting" with Death and Sheol, 1 Corinthians "victory" and "sting" with Death. 1 Corinthians 15:26 calls death "The last enemy to be destroyed", Revelation 20:14 has "Death and Hades" "thrown into the lake of fire", and 2 Corinthians 5:4 has "our mortality" "swallowed up by life".

rows.title: Tears wiped away; no more weeping or crying

The Prophets: The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears from every face
The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her
Revelation: Revelation 7:17
God will wipe away every tear from their eyes
Revelation 21:4
He will wipe away every tear from their eyes
Revelation 21:4
there will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain

rows.alike: Isaiah 25:8 ("The Lord GOD will wipe away the tears") and Revelation 7:17 ("God will wipe away every tear") name who will wipe them away, and Revelation 21:4 says "He will wipe away every tear"; Isaiah 65:19 and Revelation 21:4 both say "crying" will be no more.
rows.different: Isaiah 25:8 has "the tears from every face", Revelation "every tear from their eyes". Isaiah 65:19 says "weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her", of Jerusalem; Revelation 21:4 lists "death or mourning or crying or pain"; Isaiah 35:10 has "sorrow and sighing will flee" as "the redeemed of the LORD will return and enter Zion with singing".

rows.title: God's dwelling with them; they will be His people

The Prophets: My dwelling place will be with them; I will be their God, and they will be My people
I will be their God, and they will be My people
they will become My people. I will dwell among you
I will dwell among the Israelites forever
I will dwell among them forever
Psalms & elsewhere: I will dwell among the Israelites and be their God
I will make My dwelling place among you
I will walk among you and be your God, and you will be My people
I will dwell among the Israelites and will not abandon My people Israel
The letters: I will dwell with them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they will be My people
Revelation: Revelation 21:3
the dwelling place of God is with man, and He will dwell with them. They will be His people

rows.alike: Exodus 29:45, Leviticus 26:11, 1 Kings 6:13, Ezekiel 37:27, 43:7 and 43:9, Zechariah 2:11, 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:3 each say God will dwell, or have His dwelling place, among or with a people: "I will dwell among the Israelites" (Exodus 29:45; 1 Kings 6:13), "I will dwell among them forever" (Ezekiel 43:9), "My dwelling place will be with them" (Ezekiel 37:27), "I will dwell with them" (2 Corinthians 6:16), "He will dwell with them" (Revelation 21:3). Leviticus 26:12, Jeremiah 31:33, Ezekiel 37:27, Zechariah 2:11, 2 Corinthians 6:16 and Revelation 21:3 add that they will be His people.
rows.different: Exodus has "among the Israelites", Zechariah 2:11 "many nations will join themselves to the LORD", and Revelation 21:3 "the dwelling place of God is with man"; the earlier passages speak as "I", Revelation as "He". Leviticus 26:12 has "I will walk among you" and 2 Corinthians 6:16 "walk among them"; 2 Corinthians gives the words with "As God has said" and "we are the temple of the living God".

rows.title: I will be his God, and he will be My son

Psalms & elsewhere: I will raise up your descendant after you
I will be his Father, and he will be My son
I will be his Father, and he will be My son
The letters: I will be a Father to you, and you will be My sons and daughters, says the Lord Almighty
Revelation: Revelation 21:7
The one who overcomes will inherit all things, and I will be his God, and he will be My son

rows.alike: All have God saying "I will be" with a son: "he will be My son" (2 Samuel 7:14; 1 Chronicles 17:13; Revelation 21:7) and "you will be My sons and daughters" (2 Corinthians 6:18).
rows.different: 2 Samuel 7:14 has "his Father", said of the descendant God will raise up ("I will raise up your descendant after you", 7:12); 2 Corinthians has "a Father to you" and "sons and daughters"; Revelation 21:7 has "his God", said of "The one who overcomes", who "will inherit all things".

rows.title: The holy city, Jerusalem; nothing unclean will enter

The Prophets: O Jerusalem, holy city! For the uncircumcised and unclean will no longer enter you
The unclean will not travel it
The letters: the Jerusalem above is free, and she is our mother
you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem
Revelation: Revelation 21:2
the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God
Revelation 3:12
the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from My God
Revelation 21:27
But nothing unclean will ever enter it

rows.alike: Isaiah 52:1 calls Jerusalem "holy city" and Revelation 21:2 has "the holy city, the new Jerusalem"; Isaiah 52:1 says the "unclean will no longer enter you" and Revelation 21:27 "nothing unclean will ever enter it". Galatians, Hebrews and Revelation each name a Jerusalem with heaven or what is above: "the Jerusalem above", "the heavenly Jerusalem", "coming down out of heaven".
rows.different: Isaiah 52:1 calls to Zion, "Awake, awake, clothe yourself with strength", and Isaiah 35:8 says "The unclean will not travel" a highway, "the Way of Holiness"; Galatians says "she is our mother", Hebrews "you have come to Mount Zion", and Revelation "I saw" it "coming down out of heaven from God".

rows.title: A bride adorned for her husband

The Prophets: He has clothed me with garments of salvation and wrapped me in a robe of righteousness
as a bride adorns herself with her jewels
as a bridegroom rejoices over his bride, so your God will rejoice over you
Revelation: Revelation 19:7
the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His bride has made herself ready
Revelation 19:8
She was given clothing of fine linen, bright and pure
Revelation 21:2
prepared as a bride adorned for her husband

rows.alike: Isaiah 61:10 has "a bride adorns herself" and Revelation 21:2 "a bride adorned for her husband"; Isaiah 62:5 has a bridegroom who "rejoices over his bride" and Revelation 19:7 "the marriage of the Lamb". Both speak of clothing: "garments of salvation" and "a robe of righteousness" in Isaiah, "clothing of fine linen, bright and pure" in Revelation.
rows.different: In Isaiah the bride is a comparison ("as a bride") for the speaker whom "He has clothed", and 62:5 says "your God will rejoice over you"; Revelation 21:2 has "the holy city, the new Jerusalem" "prepared as a bride", and 19:8 says "the fine linen she wears is the righteous acts of the saints".

rows.title: Its light, its open gates, and the nations

The Prophets: Nations will come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn
Your gates will always stand open; they will never be shut, day or night
so that the wealth of the nations may be brought into you
No longer will the sun be your light by day
the LORD will be your everlasting light
Revelation: Revelation 21:23
the city has no need of sun or moon to shine on it, because the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp
Revelation 21:24
By its light the nations will walk, and into it the kings of the earth will bring their glory
Revelation 21:25
Its gates will never be shut at the end of the day, because there will be no night there
Revelation 21:26
into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations
Revelation 22:5
they will have no need for the light of a lamp or of the sun

rows.alike: Isaiah 60 and Revelation 21 both say gates "will never be shut" ("Your gates"; "Its gates"), that nations and kings come to or walk by the light ("Nations will come to your light"; "By its light the nations will walk"), that what the nations have is brought in ("the wealth of the nations may be brought into you"; "into the city will be brought the glory and honor of the nations"), and that the sun is not the light: "No longer will the sun be your light by day"; "the city has no need of sun or moon".
rows.different: Isaiah 60:19 says "the LORD will be your everlasting light", Revelation 21:23 "the glory of God illuminates the city, and the Lamb is its lamp". Isaiah's gates are open "day or night"; Revelation's are not shut "because there will be no night there". Isaiah has "wealth", Revelation "glory and honor".

rows.title: A river flowing out

Genesis: Genesis 2:10
a river flowed out of Eden to water the garden
The Prophets: water flowing from under the threshold of the temple
living water will flow out from Jerusalem
Gospels & Acts: Streams of living water will flow from within him
Revelation: Revelation 22:1
a river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb

rows.alike: Each has water flowing out: "a river flowed out of Eden", "water flowing from under the threshold of the temple", "living water will flow out from Jerusalem", "Streams of living water will flow from within him", "a river of the water of life ... flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb". Genesis 2:10 and Revelation 22:1 both have "a river".
rows.different: It flows "out of Eden" (Genesis 2:10), "from under the threshold of the temple" (Ezekiel 47:1), "out from Jerusalem" (Zechariah 14:8), "from within him" (John 7:38, "as the Scripture has said"), and "from the throne of God and of the Lamb" (Revelation 22:1). Genesis's river "branched into four headwaters", Zechariah's runs "half of it toward the Eastern Sea and the other half toward the Western Sea", and Revelation's is "as clear as crystal".

rows.title: The tree of life

Genesis: Genesis 2:9
in the middle of the garden were the tree of life
Genesis 3:22
take also from the tree of life, and eat, and live forever
Genesis 3:24
a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life
Psalms & elsewhere: She is a tree of life to those who embrace her
The fruit of the righteous is a tree of life
desire fulfilled is a tree of life
A soothing tongue is a tree of life
Revelation: Revelation 2:7
I will grant the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God
Revelation 22:2
On either side of the river stood a tree of life
Revelation 22:14
Blessed are those who wash their robes, so that they may have the right to the tree of life
Revelation 22:19
God will take away his share in the tree of life and the holy city

rows.alike: Genesis, Proverbs and Revelation all have the words "tree of life". Genesis and Revelation both speak of eating from it: "take also from the tree of life, and eat" (Genesis 3:22), "eat from the tree of life" (Revelation 2:7).
rows.different: In Genesis and Revelation "the tree of life" is a tree with a place: "in the middle of the garden" (Genesis 2:9), "in the Paradise of God" (Revelation 2:7), "On either side of the river" (Revelation 22:2); Genesis 3:24 has "a whirling sword of flame to guard the way to the tree of life", and Revelation speaks of "the right to the tree of life" (22:14). In Proverbs four things are each called "a tree of life": "She" (3:18), "The fruit of the righteous" (11:30), "desire fulfilled" (13:12) and "A soothing tongue" (15:4).

rows.title: Fruit each month and leaves for healing

The Prophets: Along both banks of the river, fruit trees of all kinds will grow
Each month they will bear fruit
Their fruit will be used for food and their leaves for healing
Revelation: Revelation 22:2
On either side of the river stood a tree of life
Revelation 22:2
bearing twelve kinds of fruit and yielding a fresh crop for each month
Revelation 22:2
the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations

rows.alike: Both have fruit-bearing on both sides of a river ("Along both banks of the river"; "On either side of the river"), fruit every month ("Each month they will bear fruit"; "a fresh crop for each month"), and leaves "for healing" or "for the healing of the nations".
rows.different: Ezekiel has "fruit trees of all kinds" whose "leaves will not wither", fed by "the water from the sanctuary"; Revelation has "a tree of life, bearing twelve kinds of fruit", and healing "of the nations".

rows.title: No longer any curse

Genesis: Genesis 3:14
cursed are you above all livestock and every beast of the field
Genesis 3:17
cursed is the ground because of you; through toil you will eat of it all the days of your life
The Prophets: Therefore a curse has consumed the earth, and its inhabitants must bear the guilt
Revelation: Revelation 22:3
No longer will there be any curse

rows.alike: Genesis 3:17 has "cursed is the ground" and Isaiah 24:6 "a curse has consumed the earth"; Revelation 22:3 says "No longer will there be any curse".
rows.different: In Genesis God speaks a curse on the serpent ("cursed are you") and on "the ground because of you", with "toil"; Isaiah 24:6 has "its inhabitants must bear the guilt"; Revelation 22:3 names no one cursed and is followed by "The throne of God and of the Lamb will be within the city".

rows.title: Let the thirsty come and drink

The Prophets: Come, all you who are thirsty, come to the waters
Come, buy wine and milk without money and without cost
Gospels & Acts: If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink
the water I give him will become in him a fount of water springing up to eternal life
Revelation: Revelation 21:6
To the thirsty I will give freely from the spring of the water of life
Revelation 22:17
let the one who is thirsty come, and the one who desires the water of life drink freely

rows.alike: Isaiah 55:1, John 7:37 and Revelation 22:17 each call the "thirsty" to "come"; Isaiah has "without cost" and Revelation "freely".
rows.different: Isaiah says "come to the waters" and "buy wine and milk without money"; John 7:37 says "come to Me and drink"; Revelation has "the water of life" and "the spring of the water of life", John 4:14 "a fount of water springing up to eternal life". In Revelation 22:17 "The Spirit and the bride say" it.

rows.title: They will see His face

Psalms & elsewhere: I will behold Your face in righteousness; when I awake
Even after my skin has been destroyed, yet in my flesh I will see God
Gospels & Acts: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God
The letters: Now we see but a dim reflection as in a mirror; then we shall see face to face
we will be like Him, for we will see Him as He is
Revelation: Revelation 22:4
They will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads

rows.alike: Psalm 17:15 has "I will behold Your face", 1 Corinthians 13:12 "face to face" and Revelation 22:4 "They will see His face"; Job 19:26 and Matthew 5:8 both have "will see God".
rows.different: Who sees differs: "I" (Psalm 17:15; Job 19:26), "the pure in heart" (Matthew 5:8), "we" (1 Corinthians; 1 John), "They" (Revelation 22:4). Job has "in my flesh" and "after my skin has been destroyed", the Psalm "when I awake", 1 Corinthians sets it after "Now we see but a dim reflection", 1 John adds "we will be like Him", and Revelation adds "His name will be on their foreheads".

rows.title: A kingdom forever; they will reign

The Prophets: I saw One like the Son of Man coming with the clouds of heaven
His kingdom is one that will never be destroyed
the saints of the Most High will receive the kingdom and possess it forever
His kingdom will be an everlasting kingdom
Psalms & elsewhere: I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever
Gospels & Acts: He will reign over the house of Jacob forever. His kingdom will never end!
you who have followed Me will also sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel
The letters: if we endure, we will also reign with Him
He hands over the kingdom to God the Father
He must reign until He has put all His enemies under His feet
Revelation: Revelation 11:15
The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever
Revelation 22:5
they will reign forever and ever

rows.alike: 2 Samuel 7:13, Daniel 7:14, Luke 1:33, Revelation 11:15 and Revelation 22:5 each speak of a kingdom or a reign without end: "the throne of his kingdom forever" (2 Samuel 7:13), "will never be destroyed" (Daniel 7:14), "His kingdom will never end" (Luke 1:33), "He will reign forever and ever" (Revelation 11:15), "they will reign forever and ever" (Revelation 22:5).
rows.different: Who reigns differs: "his kingdom" in 2 Samuel, "One like the Son of Man" and "the saints of the Most High" in Daniel, "He" over "the house of Jacob" in Luke, "we will also reign with Him" in 2 Timothy, "our Lord and of His Christ" and then "they" in Revelation; Matthew has "twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel". 1 Corinthians 15:24-25 has "He must reign until" and "He hands over the kingdom to God the Father".

rows.title: The dead will rise, to life or to judgment

The Prophets: Your dead will live; their bodies will rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust!
many who sleep in the dust of the earth will awake, some to everlasting life, but others to shame and everlasting contempt
Gospels & Acts: all who are in their graves will hear His voice
those who have done good to the resurrection of life, and those who have done evil to the resurrection of judgment
there will be a resurrection of both the righteous and the wicked
The letters: For the trumpet will sound, the dead will be raised imperishable, and we will be changed
with the trumpet of God, and the dead in Christ will be the first to rise
Revelation: Revelation 20:12
I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne
Revelation 20:12
the dead were judged according to their deeds

rows.alike: Isaiah 26:19 and Daniel 12:2 both speak of those in "the dust" who "awake"; Daniel 12:2, John 5:29 and Acts 24:15 each name two outcomes or two kinds raised: "some to everlasting life, but others to shame", "the resurrection of life" and "the resurrection of judgment", "both the righteous and the wicked". 1 Corinthians 15:52 and 1 Thessalonians 4:16 both have a trumpet.
rows.different: Daniel has "many" and John "all who are in their graves"; Isaiah has "their bodies will rise", 1 Corinthians "raised imperishable", 1 Thessalonians "the dead in Christ will be the first to rise". Revelation 20:12 has "the dead, great and small, standing before the throne" and "judged according to their deeds".

rows.title: They will shine like the stars and the sun

The Prophets: the wise will shine like the brightness of the heavens
those who lead many to righteousness will shine like the stars forever and ever
Psalms & elsewhere: those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest
Gospels & Acts: the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father

rows.alike: Daniel 12:3 and Matthew 13:43 say people "will shine like" a light of the sky; Judges 5:31 says "may those who love You shine like the sun at its brightest".
rows.different: Daniel has "the wise" and "those who lead many to righteousness", shining "like the brightness of the heavens" and "like the stars forever and ever"; Matthew has "the righteous", shining "like the sun in the kingdom of their Father"; Judges 5:31 has "those who love You" shining "like the sun at its brightest".

rows.title: The first man from the dust; the earthly and the heavenly

Genesis: Genesis 2:7
the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground
Genesis 2:7
the man became a living being
Genesis 5:3
he had a son in his own likeness, after his own image
The letters: The first man Adam became a living being
the last Adam a life-giving spirit
The first man was of the dust of the earth, the second man from heaven
just as we have borne the likeness of the earthly man, so also shall we bear the likeness of the heavenly man

rows.alike: 1 Corinthians 15:45 has "So it is written: The first man Adam became a living being"; Genesis 2:7 has "the man became a living being". Genesis 2:7 has man formed "from the dust of the ground" and 1 Corinthians 15:47 "of the dust of the earth". Genesis 5:3 and 1 Corinthians 15:49 both have "likeness".
rows.different: Genesis 2:7 has God who "breathed the breath of life into his nostrils"; 1 Corinthians 15:45 has "the last Adam a life-giving spirit" and 1 Corinthians 15:47 "the second man from heaven", which Genesis 2:7 does not have. Genesis 5:3 is Adam's son "in his own likeness"; 1 Corinthians 15:49 has "the likeness of the earthly man" and "the likeness of the heavenly man".

rows.title: A new heart and a new spirit

The Prophets: I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you
put a new spirit within them
fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit
Psalms & elsewhere: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me

rows.alike: Both join heart and spirit, and a spirit "within": "a new heart and put a new spirit within you" (Ezekiel 36:26), "a clean heart" and "a right spirit within me" (Psalm 51:10).
rows.different: Ezekiel 36:26 and 11:19 have God giving ("I will give you a new heart"); Ezekiel 18:31 tells Israel to "fashion for yourselves a new heart and a new spirit"; Psalm 51:10 is a prayer, "Create in me". Ezekiel has a "new" heart and spirit, the Psalm a "clean" heart and a "right" spirit.

rows.title: Written on hearts, not on tablets of stone

The Prophets: I will put My law in their minds and inscribe it on their hearts
I will remove your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh
Psalms & elsewhere: tablets of stone inscribed by the finger of God
The letters: written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts
I will put My laws in their minds and inscribe them on their hearts
I will put My laws in their hearts and inscribe them on their minds

rows.alike: Jeremiah 31:33 and Hebrews 8:10 both have "in their minds" and "on their hearts"; Exodus 24:12 and 31:18 and Deuteronomy 4:13, 5:22 and 9:9 have "tablets of stone", and 2 Corinthians 3:3 "not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts"; Ezekiel 36:26 sets "heart of stone" against "heart of flesh".
rows.different: Exodus 31:18 has "inscribed by the finger of God" and Exodus 24:12 "with the law and commandments I have written"; Deuteronomy 4:13 and 5:22 have "two tablets of stone" and Deuteronomy 9:9 "the tablets of the covenant"; 2 Corinthians has "written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God". Jeremiah has "My law", Hebrews "My laws", and Hebrews 10:16 reverses the order: "in their hearts" and "on their minds".

rows.title: I will pour out My Spirit

The Prophets: I will pour out My Spirit on your descendants
until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high. Then the desert will be an orchard
And afterward, I will pour out My Spirit on all people
I will put My Spirit within you
I will pour out My Spirit on the house of Israel
I will pour out My Spirit in those days
Psalms & elsewhere: poured out my spirit on you
Gospels & Acts: In the last days, God says, I will pour out My Spirit on all people
I will pour out My Spirit in those days
The letters: the washing of new birth and renewal by the Holy Spirit
This is the Spirit He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior

rows.alike: Isaiah 44:3, Joel 2:28 and 2:29, Ezekiel 39:29 and Acts 2:17 and 2:18 all have "I will pour out My Spirit"; Isaiah 32:15 has "the Spirit is poured out upon us" and Titus 3:6 "the Spirit He poured out on us".
rows.different: On whom: "your descendants" (Isaiah 44:3), "upon us from on high" (Isaiah 32:15), "all people" (Joel 2:28; Acts 2:17), "the house of Israel" (Ezekiel 39:29), "My menservants and maidservants" (Joel 2:29; Acts 2:18), "on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior" (Titus). Acts 2:17 begins "In the last days, God says"; Joel 2:28 begins "And afterward"; Joel 2:29 and Acts 2:18 have "in those days", and Acts 2:18 adds "and they will prophesy". Titus speaks in the past ("He poured out") and of "renewal by the Holy Spirit"; Ezekiel 36:27 has "put My Spirit within you", and Isaiah 32:15 adds "the desert will be an orchard".

rows.title: The new self, in the image of its Creator

Genesis: Genesis 1:27
God created man in His own image
The letters: to put off your former way of life, your old self
to put on the new self, created to be like God in true righteousness and holiness
have put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge in the image of its Creator

rows.alike: Genesis 1:27 has "created man in His own image" and Colossians 3:10 "in the image of its Creator"; Ephesians 4:24 has "created to be like God". Ephesians and Colossians both speak of putting on "the new self".
rows.different: Genesis tells what God "created", "male and female"; Ephesians tells readers "to put off" the "old self" and "to put on the new self", while Colossians says they "have put on the new self, which is being renewed". Ephesians adds "in true righteousness and holiness", Colossians "in knowledge".

rows.title: The wolf with the lamb; a covenant with the beasts

Genesis: Genesis 9:9
I now establish My covenant with you and your descendants after you
Genesis 9:10
the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth
The Prophets: The wolf will live with the lamb
the lion will eat straw like the ox
They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain
The wolf and the lamb will feed together, and the lion will eat straw like the ox
They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain
I will make a covenant for them with the beasts of the field and the birds of the air and the creatures that crawl on the ground
I will make with them a covenant of peace and rid the land of wild animals
Psalms & elsewhere: you will have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the wild animals will be at peace with you

rows.alike: Isaiah 11 and 65:25 both put the wolf with the lamb (11:6), have "the lion will eat straw like the ox" (11:7), and say "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain" (11:9). Hosea 2:18, Job 5:23 and Genesis 9:9-10 each speak of a covenant and the animals: "the beasts of the field and the birds of the air", "the wild animals will be at peace with you", "the birds, the livestock, and every beast of the earth".
rows.different: Isaiah 11:6 has "The wolf will live with the lamb", 65:25 "will feed together". Genesis 9 has God's covenant "with you and your descendants" and with the animals; Hosea's is made "for them with the beasts", Job's is "with the stones of the field", and Ezekiel 34:25's "covenant of peace" will instead "rid the land of wild animals".

rows.title: Dust the serpent's food

Genesis: Genesis 3:14
On your belly will you go, and dust you will eat, all the days of your life
The Prophets: the food of the serpent will be dust
They will lick the dust like a snake

rows.alike: Genesis 3:14 says to the serpent "dust you will eat", and Isaiah 65:25 says "the food of the serpent will be dust".
rows.different: Genesis 3:14 is spoken to the serpent with "cursed are you" and "all the days of your life"; Isaiah 65:25 sets it beside "The wolf and the lamb will feed together"; Micah 7:17 says of others, "They will lick the dust like a snake".

rows.title: Build houses and live in them; plant vineyards and eat

The Prophets: They will build houses and dwell in them; they will plant vineyards and eat their fruit
No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat
they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities. They will plant vineyards and drink their wine
Psalms & elsewhere: You will build a house but will not live in it. You will plant a vineyard but will not enjoy its fruit

rows.alike: All three pair building and dwelling with planting vineyards: "build houses and dwell in them" and "plant vineyards" (Isaiah 65:21), "rebuild and inhabit" and "plant vineyards" (Amos 9:14), "build a house" and "plant a vineyard" (Deuteronomy 28:30).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 28:30 has the reverse: "but will not live in it" and "but will not enjoy its fruit", and Isaiah 65:22 says "No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit". Isaiah has "eat their fruit" and Amos "drink their wine" and "the ruined cities"; Isaiah 65:22 adds "as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people".

rows.title: A new covenant; sins remembered no more

The Prophets: I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah
It will not be like the covenant I made with their fathers
I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more
I will make a covenant of peace with them; it will be an everlasting covenant
Gospels & Acts: This cup is the new covenant in My blood, which is poured out for you
The letters: This cup is the new covenant in My blood
ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit
I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah
I will forgive their iniquities and will remember their sins no more

rows.alike: Jeremiah 31:31 and 34 and Hebrews 8:8 and 12 have the same words: "I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah" and "will remember their sins no more"; Isaiah 43:25 has "remembers your sins no more". Luke 22:20 and 1 Corinthians 11:25 both have "This cup is the new covenant in My blood", and Hebrews 8:13, 9:15 and 12:24 have "a new covenant".
rows.different: Jeremiah sets it against "the covenant I made with their fathers"; Hebrews introduces the words with "God found fault with the people and said". Isaiah 43:25 has "blots out your transgressions for My own sake". Luke adds "which is poured out for you", 1 Corinthians "in remembrance of Me", and 2 Corinthians 3:6 "not of the letter but of the Spirit"; Ezekiel 37:26 has "a covenant of peace" and "an everlasting covenant". Hebrews 8:13 has "He has made the first one obsolete", and Hebrews 9:15 and 12:24 have "mediator of a new covenant".

rows.title: Where righteousness dwells

The Prophets: until the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high
Then justice will inhabit the wilderness, and righteousness will dwell in the fertile field
The work of righteousness will be peace

rows.alike: Isaiah 32:16 says "righteousness will dwell" and 2 Peter 3:13 "where righteousness dwells".
rows.different: Isaiah has righteousness "in the fertile field" and "justice" in "the wilderness", after "the Spirit is poured out upon us from on high" (32:15); 2 Peter has "a new heaven and a new earth".
